name: LanguageSwitcher
description: Compact language selector: a current-language trigger that fans out the other locales as a button group.

ariaRequirements: each option has an accessible name (aria-label)
a11y.reviewedNote: Verified 2026-06-02: role=group + aria-label; trigger exposes aria-expanded/aria-controls/aria-current; options are native buttons with aria-label. Escape and outside-click close; reduced motion swaps the fan for a fade. KeyboardToggle play function drives open-via-trigger / close-via-Escape and passes axe; Default/Example/Playground pass axe with test:error; light + dark verified in Storybook.

dense: Locale toggle: current-language button fans out a tray of other locales (spring motion, reduced-motion fade; closed tray inert); Escape/outside click close; controlled currentLang + onLanguageChange

usage.description: LanguageSwitcher is the site-chrome locale control: the current language shows as a compact button that fans out a tray of the other locales on demand. It is controlled — update your i18n instance in `onLanguageChange` and pass the new `currentLang` back. Each option carries its own `ariaLabel`, announced in the target language; the closed tray is `inert` so hidden options can never take focus, and Escape or an outside click closes it.

bestPractices.description: Write each option's ariaLabel in its target language ("Vaihda kieli suomeksi") so users who need that language understand it.
Keep it controlled: change the i18n language inside onLanguageChange and feed the new currentLang back down.
Use short locale labels (EN/FI/SV); the fan tray is chrome, not a settings page.
Trust the built-in Escape, outside-click close, and inert tray — do not wrap it in another disclosure.
Do not use flags as the only label; flags name countries, not languages.
Do not bury language choice in a settings modal on public pages — it is a first-visit need and belongs in the header.
